beats.caption: A brushless outrunner motor. The outer shell, called the bell, turns with the propeller. The middle part is fixed to the drone.

onScreen.text: Three wires from the speed controller (ESC)

beats.caption: Cut the bell open. Permanent magnets line the inside of the bell. The fixed stator in the middle carries coils of copper wire.

onScreen.text: Coil of copper wire on each tooth

beats.caption: The parts, pulled apart along the shaft. Two bearings hold the shaft, so the bell turns freely round the stator.

onScreen.text: Coil of copper wire on each tooth

beats.caption: This stator has 12 coils, one on each tooth. The bell has 7 magnets with the north pole facing in and 7 with the south pole facing in. They alternate round the ring.
The coils are joined in three groups, called phases. This is phase A: two pairs of neighbouring coils on opposite sides. In each pair, the two coils are wound in opposite directions.
Phase B is the next two pairs.
Phase C is the last two pairs. Current in a phase makes its coils electromagnets. In each pair, one coil face is north and one is south. They pull unlike magnet poles and push like poles.
In six-step control, the speed controller energizes two phases at a time and changes the pair in a repeating order. The stator's magnetic field turns, and the magnets follow it.
Seen from above without the bell: the ring of magnets turns round the fixed coils. One turn of the bell takes 7 electrical cycles, one for each pair of magnets.
Swap any two of the three wires and the order reverses: the motor turns the other way.

onScreen.text: Three wires from the speed controller (ESC)

beats.caption: What the engine checked: the turning of the bell, and the counts of coils and magnets. Currents, magnetic forces and torque are not computed.

title: Inside a drone's brushless motor (outrunner)
